findings.source_passage: Finally, though, as will soon be revealed, its contents partly comprise the most delicate oil; yet, you are now to be apprised of the nature of the substance which so impregnably invests all that apparent effeminacy.
findings.why_it_matters: This transition sentence sets up the contrast between the delicate spermaceti within and the impregnable toughness without — the 'apparent effeminacy' framing is interpretively loaded and rhetorically distinctive. Its omission erases the paradox Melville is building.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence beginning 'Finally, though, as will soon be revealed…' between the 'one wad' statement and the orange-rind analogy.

findings.source_passage: it has hypothetically occurred to me, I say, that those mystical lung-celled honeycombs there may possibly have some hitherto unknown and unsuspected connexion
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, second occurrence of 'hypothetically occurred to me'
findings.why_it_matters: Melville's deliberate rhetorical device of repeating 'it has hypothetically occurred to me, I say' is a voice-establishing tic that enacts the narrator's hedged, self-conscious speculation. The draft drops the repeated phrase and 'I say,' flattening the self-aware rhetorical register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the repeated 'I say' and the full doublet 'hitherto unknown and unsuspected' to preserve Melville's self-conscious hedging tone.

findings.source_passage: when I shall show you some of his more inconsiderable braining feats; I trust you will have renounced all ignorant incredulity, and be ready to abide by this
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, before the Isthmus of Darien sentence
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'renounced all ignorant incredulity' is part of the chapter's climactic rhetorical build — the narrator demanding the reader surrender disbelief before the Darien hyperbole. The draft collapses this to 'be ready to abide by this,' losing the confrontational register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I trust you will have renounced all ignorant incredulity, and be ready to abide by this' before the Darien sentence.

summary: The draft is largely faithful and preserves all major signature passages including the Darien hyperbole and the salamander-giants coda, but loses three medium-weight voice and interpretive moments: the 'apparent effeminacy' transitional paradox, the doubled 'hypothetically occurred to me, I say' rhetorical tic, and the 'renounced all ignorant incredulity' climactic build.
